headline: Low prompt-injection and data-leakage risk; pdf.js can ingest PDFs while the prompt-engineering repo is a non-runnable content source, so interaction is mostly manual and limited.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a non-runnable content-writing repo with no I/O surfaces, while profile B processes PDF files and can run browsers. The only plausible bridge is manual copy/paste or file handoff, so A cannot directly inject B by default. B’s PDF parsing could still be influenced if an operator feeds A-derived text into it.
conditions: IF an operator copies A-derived text into B’s PDF-processing workflow, injection becomes possible.
IF B is configured to treat extracted PDF text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer behavior.
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate workspaces.
Do not copy untrusted A content into B without review.
Render A outputs as plain text, not executable instructions.
Add a manual provenance check before B consumes any A-derived artifact.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no filesystem or network surfaces; B touches PDF documents and has network egress set to none. There is no documented shared workspace or authenticated principal, so leakage is not evidenced. The remaining risk is limited to operator-mediated transfer of PDFs or text between the two.
conditions: IF the operator places sensitive PDFs into both agents’ workflows, both can observe the same content.
IF a shared filesystem is introduced, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Use separate folders for A and B.
Avoid placing sensitive PDFs in A’s workspace.
Confirm B’s network egress remains disabled.
Delete temporary exports after review.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no declared write, network, or concurrency capabilities, and B only declares browser-based tests with multiple-instance support plus PDF-file I/O. There is no shared mutable resource or overlapping write surface in the profiles, so a capability conflict is not plausible from the documented pair.
conditions: IF A is later given write access to the same directory as B, conflict risk would need reevaluation.
IF B is extended with shared mutable state, locking would become relevant.
mitigations: Keep A read-only.
Avoid mounting a shared writable directory.
Run B with isolated test inputs.
Reassess if either agent gains filesystem write access.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a content-writing source that can produce persuasive but unverified material, and B is a document processor that may render or act on PDF-derived content. Because B’s sandboxing is browser-based tests rather than a verified verification layer, A’s output could flow into B without strong validation. The pathway exists in default use if operators chain them.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated text or citations as authoritative input, cascading error is possible.
IF the operator uses B to render A’s outputs without independent fact-checking, errors can propagate.
mitigations: Require a second-pass human review.
Mark A outputs as untrusted drafts.
Have B verify claims against source PDFs before acting.
Separate generation from validation steps.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent. A is an open-source content repo with no data classes touched, and B only lists PDF documents with network egress none. Without a documented regulated-data flow, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into either workflow, compliance must be rechecked.
IF a deployment policy imposes residency or retention constraints, those constraints must be mapped separately.
mitigations: Do not process regulated data until policies are reviewed.
Document data classes before deployment.
Confirm retention settings for any PDF workflow.
Reassess if either agent is assigned compliance-sensitive data.
